fix.shows: Deccan Herald's editorial says the special summary revision in the states where the intensive revision has ended is an opportunity to repair the damage it says the intensive revision did. It gives Karnataka's electorate as falling from 5.54 crore to 4.55 crore after the intensive revision, more than 99 lakh fewer names, with the final roll of the summary revision due on 20 January 2027. It says the Commission has clarified that voters need not establish a link with the rolls of 2002, and reads that as an admission that the intensive revision imposed unreasonable burdens on voters. It says the remedy comes too late for voters in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Bihar, where the revision was held close to the elections, and that in West Bengal nearly 21 lakh appeals against deletions remain pending months after polling. It asks Karnataka's parties to use their booth level agents to see that every eligible voter is restored to the rolls, and says the Congress did not sustain its campaign. It notes the Karnataka High Court's stay of the investigations in the FIRs against BJP booth level agents accused of filing Form 7 objections in bulk, says the court's view that the registration officer must first complete the statutory process may be legally defensible, and sets beside it the Commission's acknowledgement of more than 91,000 Form 7 applications, many in bulk, and its position that no voter has been deleted on them. It asks that the Commission's new safeguards, among them scrutiny of bulk objections, hearings and reasoned orders before any deletion, be enforced in the summary revision.
